newsitem.title: USA: Clinton will fight U.S. balanced budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton will fight U.S. balanced budget amendment.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will fight a proposed amendment to the Constitution that requires a balanced budget, new White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles said on Sunday.

"We are against it," Bowles said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" program. "We are for a balanced budget," he said, citing the lowering of the budget deficit since Clinton first took office four years ago.
"We don't think it's right to muck around with the Constitution," Bowles said.
Clinton has promised to work with the Republican-controlled Congress to balance the budget by the year 2002.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told the Senate Judiciary Committee on Friday that the White House and Congress were making progress on balancing the budget.

But, he said "a balanced budget amendment is a threat to our economic health, will expose our economy to unacceptable risks and should not be adopted. It would seriously increase the risk of default on national debt."
It takes a two-thirds majority in both the House of Representatives and Senate to pass a constitutional amendment and to send it to the states for ratification.

The House passed a balanced budget amendment in 1995 but it failed by one vote in the Senate. Republican leaders have pledged to try again to pass the amendment early this year but its chances are uncertain because House Republicans lost nine seats last November. Senate Republicans gained two seats.
